bio: Working harbour lighthouse in Madang, also the memorial to WWII coastwatchers who reported Japanese movements.
Busy central market in Madang where people bring Highlands produce to sell, mostly fruit and vegetables.
Road-free island a five-minute boat ride from Madang, with two villages, gardens and a lagoon beach.
Oval volcanic island in the Bismarck Sea with an active twin-caldera volcano and a mountain view down to Madang.
Commonwealth WWII cemetery beside Lae Botanic Gardens, begun in 1944 and holding the Lae Memorial to the missing.
Walk-through rainforest aviary with birds of paradise at Unitech in Lae; reported run-down, so check before going.
Gold dredges left in the Bulolo jungle, every part airlifted in by Junkers aircraft before dredging ended in 1965.
Active volcano above Rabaul reached by road, with hot springs and ash deposits; climbs start here with a guide.
Volcano observatory on Mount Tavanabatir with a lookout over Rabaul town, the bay and the volcano.
WWII tunnel near Mount Vulcan with Japanese barges still inside, down a rough unmarked track at Karavia.
1937 New Guinea Club building turned museum of Rabaul's history, with many photographs, opposite Yamamoto's bunker.
Commonwealth war cemetery near Kokopo for WWII servicemen from many countries, with a Japanese war memorial.
Museum in central Kokopo of Japanese war relics, with a few photographs, opposite the waterfront golf course.
Group of 13 islands about 45 minutes by boat from Kokopo, visited for diving, snorkelling and picnics.
Bay off Kimbe with over 900 fish and 400 coral species, reached by dive boat from Kimbe or Walindi.
Southern trailhead of the 96 km Kokoda Track, 50 km from Port Moresby; treks need a licensed operator and permit.
Site of the 1942 Battle of Isurava on the Kokoda Track, with a memorial and museum reached only on foot.
Coastal Oro Province village with WWII relics and a memorial plaque to the 32nd Red Arrow Division at its entrance.
Coastal village in Oro Province where Japanese forces landed in 1942; visited for WWII relics, with a local guide.
Sepik town whose district is known for forward-leaning haus tambaran spirit houses; ask permission before entering.
River reached from Wewak by motor-canoe, with day trips, overnight expeditions and village stays.
Island 30 minutes by boat from Wewak with waterfalls, snorkelling and natural hot springs.
Small island reached by boat from Wewak, one of four within an hour of town.
Peace park near Wewak where General Adachi signed the Japanese surrender in 1945, with some tunnels still open.
Remote lake and wetland in Western Province for birdwatching and fishing, reached by light aircraft then boat.
Ramsar wetland of 590,000 hectares on the Indonesian border, reached by charter flight to Bensbach Wildlife Lodge.
